sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:87902
Court No. - 91

Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 29923 of 2021
Applicant :- Indu Sharma

Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 2 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Kamal Kishor Mishra,Vikas Tiwari
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Garun Pal Singh,Saumya Tripathi
Hon'ble Prashant Kumar,J.
1.
Hear Sri Kamal Kishor, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri S.K. Chandraul, learned A.G.A. for the State, Sri G.P. Singh, learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 and perused the record.

2. The instant application under Section 482 Cr.P.c. has been filed seeking quashing order dated 28-08-2019 passed by Judicial Magistrate, Mathura in Complaint No. 165 of 2019 and Order dated 27-09-2021 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge, Mathura in Revision No. 386 of 2019,
under Section 203 Cr.P.C. P.s. Mahila Thana, district Mathura.
3.

Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant had filed an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. on 14-04-2019 and the same was rejected vide order dated 28-08-2019 passed by Judicial Magistrate, Mathura on the ground that earlier there was no complaint filed by the applicant regarding violence, hence he has no reason to entertain application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. Against which the applicant preferred a revision being Criminal Revision No. 386 of 2019 and the learned Additional Sessions Judge after considering the facts and circumstances in detail was pleased to reject the criminal revision vide order dated 27-09-2021.

Both the orders are Indu Sharma vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164942018/
1 under challenge in the instant application.

sentences.text: It is submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant had earlier filed a complaint regarding violence.
Further submission is that the applicant is wife of the opposite party no.2, who is continuously beating her up.

4. Sri G.P. Singh learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 has vehemently opposed the instant application and contended that the applicant and the opposite party no.2 has been married for the last 45 years and presently the opposite party no.2 is living in Vrindavan Ashram.
He further submits that the applicant has herself thrown him out of the house and there is no illegality in the order passed by the court concerned, which requires any interference by this Court.

5. Heard counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6.

The learned Magistrate in its order dated 28-08-2019 submits that the complainant was married to Suresh Chandra Sharma (opposite party no.2) 45 years ago and has faced cruel treatment and physical abuse from him, as well as abusive behaviour from Ramesh Chandra and Umesh Sharma.
Despite supporting statements from witnesses, the court noted the lack of substantial evidence or medical records of abuse over the years.
The court found no prima facie case against the opposite parties under sections 498A, 452, 308, 342, 325, 323, 504, 120B, and 506 IPC.

Thus, the complaint was dismissed under section 203 CrPC., which was confirmed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Mathura in its order dated 27-09-2021.
7.
In view of above, I see no illegality in both the orders passed by the court concerned.
The instant application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. is devoid of merits and is accordingly dismissed.

Order Date :- 15.5.2024 pks  Indu Sharma vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164942018/
